---
title: "Simulation-Based Inference"
format: gfm
---

Simulation-based methods provide an alternative to traditional statistical inference. Instead of relying on theoretical asymptotics, we use simulations to directly interact with the hypothesized data-generating processes. Because of this, simulation-based inference is a computation-focused approach to statistical inference.

Methods include:

- Monte Carlo simulation of probability distributions
- Permutation hypothesis tests
- Bootstrapped confidence intervals
- Simulated residuals for model diagnostic tests
- Marginal effects approach to estimating causal effects
